title: Verifier-Side Silent Failures: A Taxonomy and a Negative-Control Test Method for Automated Verifiers in Agentic AI Governance
description:
Automated verifiers — CI gates, test harnesses, compliance checkers, AI-agent output validators — can fail in a way that is structurally invisible: the verification step reports success while the property being checked was never actually exercised. We call these verifier-side silent failures. Building on a prior catalog of fourteen silent-failure modes, this paper (1) taxonomizes the verifier-side subset, (2) derives a negative-control test method in which every self-check of a verifier must carry a deliberately broken twin whose expected failure is asserted, and (3) demonstrates the method on a worked example: gate register Q0-Q6 from a regulatory annex (FG-TIDA use-case), cross-walked against four silent-failure cases and three simulation profiles (ordinary, defended, complete).

The shared root cause is that the absence of evidence is recorded as evidence of absence of a problem. Two mechanical consequences follow: a missing check must enter the exit code, and no negative control means no evidence. We position the method against related work on test oracles, TOCTTOU in agentic pipelines, and pre-registered intervention-based agent evaluation.
